title: Vegan Peppermint Chocolate Cupcakes
shortDescription: Rich vegan chocolate cupcakes with peppermint frosting, ready in 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These vegan peppermint chocolate cupcakes taste like a holiday candy cane dipped in dark chocolate. The cake is moist and deeply chocolatey, made with cocoa and coconut milk instead of eggs or dairy. On top sits a fluffy coconut milk frosting with just enough peppermint essence to feel festive, not toothpaste-like. I tested this batch three times over one December weekend, adjusting the peppermint drop by drop. Too much and the frosting tastes medicinal. The amount below hits a clean, cool mint note that pairs well with the cocoa. This recipe works for holiday parties, cookie exchanges, or any day you want chocolate mint without dairy or eggs. It also freezes well unfrosted, so you can bake ahead for busy weeks.
ingredients: 1 cup full fat canned coconut milk, well shaken
1/3 cup neutral oil (canola or melted coconut oil)
2 tbsp coconut milk (from a second can, chilled and firm)
1/2 tsp peppermint essence, or to taste
Crushed candy canes or vegan chocolate shavings, for topping
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, cocoa powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk coconut milk, sugar, oil, vinegar, and vanilla until smooth.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Stir just until no dry streaks remain.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
Beat vegan butter until fluffy, about 1 minute. Add powdered sugar in two batches, beating well after each.
Add coconut milk and peppermint essence. Beat 2 minutes until light and spreadable.
Once cupcakes are fully cool, pipe or spread frosting on top. Finish with crushed candy canes.
tips: Chill the second can of coconut milk overnight so the thick cream sits on top for frosting.
Add peppermint essence a few drops at a time and taste as you go. It is stronger than peppermint extract.
Frost cupcakes only after they are completely cool, or the frosting will slide off.
Store frosted cupcakes in the fridge and let them sit 15 minutes at room temperature before serving.

faq.question: Can I use peppermint extract instead of peppermint essence?
faq.answer: Yes, but peppermint extract is usually weaker. Start with double the amount and taste before adding more.

faq.question: Why is my coconut milk frosting runny?
faq.answer: The coconut milk was likely not chilled long enough. Chill the can at least 8 hours so the cream firms up before you scoop it.

faq.question: Can I make these cupcakes ahead for a holiday party?
faq.answer: Bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store them unfrosted at room temperature in a sealed container. Frost the day you serve them.

faq.question: Are these cupcakes nut-free?
faq.answer: Yes, as long as your vegan butter and chocolate garnish are nut-free. Always check labels if you are baking for allergies.

conclusion: These vegan peppermint chocolate cupcakes bring holiday flavor without dairy or eggs. Bake the cake ahead, chill your coconut milk, and frost them fresh for your next gathering.
